title: Saving for a picnic and winning over his father's cousin
summary: Ory saved fish-fry money to give a baseball-park picnic; the relative who doubted him changed his mind after seeing the crowd at a party.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: No relative. Well, were you able to make some money from these little operations?
Yes, I did. I was the leader, the promoter, bookkeeper, and the treasure. And the fish fryer. The fish fryer.
But he didn't stay a fish fryer long. He got girls to take over that work.
Oh, well, I was able to pay... Good little health, huh?
Mm-hmm.
Free health. I was able to pay him 50 cents a night. Well, then I was a big shot, didn't you? Sure. Yeah.
Well, were you able to save some money and so on? Would you...

Well, I saved the money until I got enough money, then I promoted a big picnic at a baseball game. An Orlean team came to play the country boys, and one of the... The park, my dad, is his first cousin, and I told him what I wanted to do, you know? Yeah. And I went to buy a real instrument, and so...
What did you buy? What instrument?

Real. That's what we're using today. I know. With what? With seven. Seven instrument. Oh, you wanted to buy instruments for everybody, you mean? Yeah. Oh, yeah. Oh. I had taken the money. I accumulated on the fish fryer, and I saved it. I kept adding to it every week. We'd play and have our fish fryer. Uh-huh. When I had enough money, I ate for the park and have a picnic after the ball game. While the game was going on, while the game was going on, while I still was selling beer and stuff, you know, and food. So they gave me everything free. When I found out what I wanted to do, my dad was coming and his partner on the plantation and the grocery store. They gave me everything I wanted. Beer and all the food and all the meat. They opened everything for me.
But you might tell what brought that on. He didn't believe in your music at first.

Yeah, I know. My dad, his first cousin, wanted me to work on the plantation after my dad had died. So I didn't like plantation work. It was a great lost tower farm. You know, my dad had died. Was sick at the time. And so he said he didn't thought I was any good.
Because he wanted to play music instead of learning how to run a plantation.
He wanted to get my job as a boss or overseer, you know.

Yes. He and his son were the only two males in the family on the Ory's plantation. Oh, I see. And it was the idea that he and the first cousin's son would eventually run the plantation as the father got old enough to not be able to do everything himself. So his female cousins, to get their father on his side, gave a party and hired his band. And when Daddy saw how all the guests loved his music from there on in, he was on Ed's side and realized he wasn't trying to get out of work after all. But he had something that should be used.
What kind of instruments did you buy when you bought real instruments? What did you buy? I showed them. I finished down there the night of the dance of the big party.
Yeah.

He came up to me. He said, you know, I'm sorry. He told me in French that he accused me of being a lazy boy. He said, you know, everyone is good for something in this world. That's right. Yeah. He said, anything I can help you, let me know.
He talked to you in French. Yeah. At this time, French was your main language. That's right.
Parisian times, too. He couldn't speak English at all.
He couldn't speak English at all. My dad didn't either. He couldn't. So you made enough on the picnic to buy the instruments. Yeah.
